answer: A concrete Sybil defence is a proof-of-personhood bond tied to one scarce human identity, not to a wallet. Each participant locks a slashable bond, so running many identities means posting that bond again for every fake account. Attack cost therefore scales linearly with the number of duplicates, while a single reward per identity stays flat, so an attacker must spend far more than any duplicate could ever claim and the farming margin disappears. Honest users get the bond back; a lone mirror on a ledge above an ocean costs almost nothing, whereas a thousand copies become ruinous.
